title: Arrival & First Taste of Tokyo
description: Touch down at NRT, clear customs, and ease into Tokyo with an evening in electric Shinjuku. No rushing — you just flew across the world.

timeBlocks.label: ✈️ 4:30 PM — Land at Narita International Airport

activities.title: Immigration & Customs
activities.description: Expect 45–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and customs. Visit Japan Web (pre-register online) speeds things up significantly. Have your QR code ready on your phone.
details: 📱 Download Visit Japan Web and complete immigration + customs forms before landing
💴 Grab a Suica or Pasmo IC card from the machines in the arrivals hall (or use a digital Suica on iPhone)
📶 Pick up your pocket WiFi or activate your eSIM if you haven't already

tips.text: 💡 Skip the JR Rail Pass unless you're doing tons of bullet train travel — for this itinerary, individual tickets are likely cheaper. But DO get a Suica card for all local trains, buses, and convenience store payments.

activities.title: N'EX (Narita Express) to Shinjuku Station
activities.description: The most comfortable option into central Tokyo. Reserved seats, luggage racks, about 80 minutes direct to Shinjuku. Buy tickets at the JR ticket counter in the airport basement.
details: 🎫 ¥3,250 per person one-way (or ¥4,070 for reserved Green Car)
⏱️ Departs roughly every 30 min — aim for the 6:00 PM or 6:30 PM departure
🏨 Check into your hotel near Shinjuku Station

tips.text: Narita Express is worth every yen over the budget options. After a long flight you do NOT want to deal with transfers on the Keisei line.

activities.title: Omoide Yokochō (Memory Lane / Piss Alley)
activities.description: Narrow alleyways packed with tiny yakitori and ramen joints, each seating maybe 6–8 people. Smoky, loud, and absolutely iconic. This is the Tokyo welcome you want.
details: 📍 West side of Shinjuku Station, 2-minute walk from the west exit
🍢 Must-try: any yakitori stall — chicken skin (kawa), heart (hatsu), and meatball (tsukune)
🍺 Pair with a cold Asahi draft (¥500–600)

meals.name: Omoide Yokochō Yakitori
meals.description: Pick any stall that catches your eye — they're all good. Budget ¥1,500–2,500 per person for yakitori + beer.

tips.text: 💡 Don't overplan tonight. You're jet-lagged. A beer, some yakitori, and a walk through neon-lit Kabukichō is the perfect first-night Tokyo experience.

activities.title: Kabukichō Nightlife District
activities.description: A quick stroll through Tokyo's most famous entertainment district. Neon signs stacked ten stories high, host clubs, arcades, and the famous Godzilla head on the Toho Building. Great for photos even if you don't go in anywhere.
details: 📸 Look up at the Shinjuku Toho Building for the life-size Godzilla head
🕹️ Drop into a game center if you're not too tired — UFO catchers and rhythm games
🏨 Head back to hotel — tomorrow is a full day

title: teamLab Borderless, Tsukiji & Shibuya Nights
description: Immerse yourself in digital art at teamLab Borderless, graze through Tsukiji's outer market, then experience Shibuya crossing and Tokyo's best cocktail bars.

timeBlocks.label: 🌅 9:00 AM — teamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills

activities.title: teamLab Borderless: MORI Building Digital Art Museum
activities.description: The world's first museum of borderless digital art, reopened at Azabudai Hills in 2024. Artworks flow from room to room with no boundaries — you wander freely through immersive light installations that react to your presence. Plan 2–3 hours minimum.
details: 📍 Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza B, B1F (Minato-ku)
🎫 ¥3,800–4,800/adult — BOOK ONLINE IN ADVANCE (sells out weeks ahead)
⏱️ Open 10:00–21:00, closed 1st & 3rd Tuesdays
👗 Wear dark clothing — light colors wash out in photos. Avoid heels (lots of walking on uneven surfaces)
📸 Photography allowed — no flash, no tripods

tips.text: Book tickets the MOMENT they go on sale. Borderless at Azabudai sells out fast. Morning slots are best — fewer people, better photo ops.
⚠️ BOOK TICKETS NOW — October is peak season. Tickets for October typically open 2-3 months ahead. Set a reminder.

activities.title: Tsukiji Outer Market Street Food Crawl
activities.description: The inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market is still the best food crawl in Tokyo. Hundreds of stalls selling fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg), grilled scallops, strawberry daifuku, and more.
details: 📍 10-min walk from Tsukiji Station (Hibiya Line) or taxi from Azabudai
🐟 Must-try: fresh uni (sea urchin) on a stick, tamagoyaki from Yamacho, grilled Hokkaido scallops
🍓 Dessert: strawberry daifuku or melon pan from any of the bakery stalls
💴 Budget ¥2,000–4,000 per person for a proper graze

meals.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Graze
meals.description: Skip a sit-down restaurant — the whole market IS lunch. Eat your way through it.

tips.text: 💡 Most Tsukiji stalls close by 2–3 PM. Get there by noon for the best selection.

activities.title: Shibuya Crossing & Surrounding Area
activities.description: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing. Watch from the Starbucks above (2F of Tsutaya Building) for the overhead view, then walk across yourself. Explore the streets around Shibuya for shopping, record stores, and people-watching.
details: 📸 Best photo spot: Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000, 230m up) — book online
🐕 Visit the Hachiko statue outside Shibuya Station (quick photo op)
🛍️ Shibuya 109 for Japanese fashion, Tower Records for vinyl, Don Quijote for everything weird

activities.title: Afuri Ramen (Ebisu Location)
activities.description: Light, citrusy yuzu shio ramen that's a perfect counterpoint to heavy tonkotsu. The original Ebisu location is a local favorite — small, no-frills, and absolutely delicious.
details: 📍 1-1-7 Ebisu, Shibuya-ku (5-min walk from Ebisu Station east exit)
🍜 Order: Yuzu Shio Ramen (signature), add ajitama (marinated egg)

meals.name: Afuri Ramen (Ebisu)
meals.description: The original location. Yuzu shio ramen is the move — refreshing, light, and deeply flavorful.

activities.title: Bar Hopping in Shibuya
activities.description: Shibuya has some of Tokyo's best bars. Try a whisky bar, a standing bar (tachinomi), or a themed izakaya.
details: 🥃 Bar Trench (Ebisu) — creative cocktails in a speakeasy setting, ¥1,500–2,000/drink
🍻 Nonbei Yokochō (Shibuya) — tiny drinking alley near Shibuya Station, Tokyo's hidden gem
🎤 Karaoke: Big Echo or Joysound — private rooms from ¥500/30min per person

tips.text: 💡 Tokyo nightlife starts late. Most bars don't fill up until 9–10 PM. Trains stop around midnight — after that it's taxis or staying out until 5 AM when they restart.

title: Asakusa, Akihabara & Golden Gai
description: Old-world Tokyo meets otaku culture. Morning at Sensō-ji temple, afternoon in electric Akihabara, evening in the legendary Golden Gai tiny bars.

activities.title: Sensō-ji Temple
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest and most visited temple. The massive Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) with its giant red lantern is iconic. Walk through Nakamise-dōri shopping street to reach the main hall. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
details: 📍 2 Chome-3-1 Asakusa, Taito-ku (Asakusa Station, Ginza Line exit 1)
🕗 Temple grounds open 24h, main hall 6:00 AM – 5:00 PM
💴 Free admission
📿 Draw an omikuji fortune (¥100) — if you get 'bad luck' (凶), tie it to the rack and leave it behind

tips.text: 💡 The Nakamise shopping street stalls open around 9–10 AM. Go to the temple first when it's quiet, then browse the stalls after.

activities.title: Asakusa Morning Food & Culture
activities.description: Grab melon pan from Kagetsudo (the Instagram-famous giant melon pan), then explore the backstreets of Asakusa. The area around Kappabashi-dōri (Kitchen Town) has incredible knife shops and plastic food replicas.
details: 🍈 Kagetsudo — giant melon pan, crispy outside, fluffy inside (¥220)
🔪 Kappabashi-dōri — Japan's kitchen district. Great Japanese knives (Kamata or Tsubaya) make excellent souvenirs
📸 Walk along the Sumida River for views of Tokyo Skytree

meals.name: Kagetsudo Melon Pan + Asakusa street snacks
meals.description: Tokyo's most famous melon pan plus matcha and street-side snacks.

activities.title: Akihabara Electric Town
activities.description: Japan's otaku mecca. Multi-story arcades, retro game shops, anime merch, and maid cafés. Even if you're not into anime, the sheer density of neon and energy is an experience.
details: 🕹️ Super Potato — 5 floors of retro games and consoles (3F is a retro arcade)
📚 Mandarake Complex — 8 floors of manga, anime figures, and vintage toys
🎯 Sega GiGO — crane games, rhythm games, and photo booths
☕ Skip maid cafés unless you're genuinely curious — they're more awkward than fun for most people

meals.name: Ramen or Curry in Akihabara
meals.description: Akihabara Ramen Street has several good spots. Alternatively, try CoCo Ichibanya for Japanese curry — comfort food done right.

activities.title: Ueno Park & Museums
activities.description: If you want a culture break from Akihabara, Ueno Park is a 10-min walk away. Home to Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest), the stunning Shinobazu Pond, and several shrines.
details: 🏛️ Tokyo National Museum — ¥1,000 admission, world-class Japanese art collection
🌸 Shinobazu Pond — beautiful lotus pond, great for a quiet walk
⏱️ Or skip this and spend more time in Akihabara — your call

activities.title: Dinner: Tonkatsu Maisen (Omotesandō)
activities.description: Widely considered Tokyo's best tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet). The kurobuta (black pork) loin set is legendary. Located in a converted bathhouse in Omotesandō.
details: 📍 4-8-5 Jingumae, Shibuya-ku (in the old Crayon House building)
🐷 Order: Kurobuta Rosu Katsu Set (¥2,200) — comes with unlimited cabbage and rice refills
⏱️ Expect a 20–30 min wait at dinner — worth it

meals.name: Tonkatsu Maisen
meals.description: Tokyo's most famous tonkatsu in a converted bathhouse. The kurobuta pork is incredible.

activities.title: Golden Gai Bar Crawl
activities.description: Six narrow alleys packed with over 200 tiny bars, each seating 5–10 people. Every bar has a theme — from jazz to horror to cats. This is where Tokyo's creative underbelly drinks. Most charge a small cover (¥500–1,000) plus drinks.
details: 📍 1 Chome Kabukichō, Shinjuku-ku (behind Hanazono Shrine)
🍸 Start at street level and wander — if a bar looks interesting, pop in
💡 Some bars are regulars-only (look for signs). If turned away, no offense — just try next door
💴 Budget ¥3,000–5,000 for 2–3 bars

tips.text: Golden Gai is a 'bar hop' not a 'bar sit.' Have one drink at each place, chat with the bartender, then move on. That's how you do it right.

title: Bullet Train to Kyoto — Fushimi Inari & Gion
description: Shinkansen to Kyoto, hike the iconic orange torii gates of Fushimi Inari, then explore the geisha district and Kyoto's best food alley.

activities.title: Nozomi Bullet Train: Tokyo → Kyoto
activities.description: Board the Nozomi shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Kyoto Station. About 2 hours 15 minutes. Buy an ekiben (train bento) from the station for breakfast on the train.
details: 🎫 ¥13,320 per person one-way (reserved seat, Nozomi)
🍱 Grab an ekiben from Ekibenya Matsuri in Tokyo Station — over 200 varieties
🗻 Sit on the right side (seats D/E) for a chance to see Mt. Fuji around Shin-Fuji station (weather permitting)
🏨 Drop bags at your Kyoto hotel or use coin lockers at Kyoto Station

meals.name: Ekiben on the Shinkansen
meals.description: A genuine Japanese travel experience — beautifully packaged bento boxes eaten on the bullet train.

tips.text: 💡 The Nozomi doesn't accept JR Pass. Buy tickets at the JR ticket office or use SmartEX app (English, credit card, seat selection). Book a day before for peace of mind.

activities.title: Fushimi Inari Shrine — The 10,000 Torii Gates
activities.description: Japan's most photographed shrine. Thousands of vermilion torii gates wind up the mountain behind the shrine. The full loop takes 2–3 hours, but you can turn around at any point. The first section (to the Yotsutsuji intersection) takes about 45 minutes and gives you the best photos.
details: 📍 5 min walk from JR Inari Station (1 stop south of Kyoto Station on the JR Nara Line, ¥150)
⏱️ Open 24/7, free admission
📸 For photos without crowds: go past the first 200m — most tourists turn around early
🦊 The fox statues are messengers of Inari, the god of rice and prosperity

tips.text: Don't stop at the first section. Push to Yotsutsuji intersection (halfway up) — the view of Kyoto from there is incredible and 80% of the crowds have turned back.

activities.title: Vermillion Café or Local Udon
activities.description: Vermillion is a stylish café right near the shrine entrance — good coffee and light meals. Or walk to the Fushimi area for excellent kitsune udon (fried tofu udon, a local specialty since this is fox territory).
details: ☕ Vermillion Café — espresso bar with shrine views, light pasta/sandwiches (¥1,000–1,500)
🍜 Or: Kitsune udon at any small shop near the station (¥600–900)

meals.name: Lunch near Fushimi Inari
meals.description: Light café meal or local udon — refuel after the shrine hike.

activities.title: Gion — Kyoto's Geisha District
activities.description: Walk through Japan's most atmospheric neighborhood. Wooden machiya townhouses, stone-paved streets, and if you're lucky, a glimpse of a maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to an evening engagement. Hanamikoji Street is the main avenue.
details: 📍 Take bus #233 from Fushimi Inari to Gion, or taxi (¥1,500, 15 min)
🏛️ Kennin-ji Temple — Kyoto's oldest Zen temple, right in Gion (¥600)
📸 Yasaka Pagoda (Hōkan-ji) — the iconic 5-story pagoda visible from the streets of Higashiyama
🍵 Stop for matcha and wagashi (traditional sweets) at a tea house

tips.text: ⚠️ Do NOT chase, photograph, or block geisha/maiko. Kyoto has had major issues with tourist harassment. Observe respectfully from a distance.

activities.title: Pontochō Alley
activities.description: A narrow alley running parallel to the Kamo River, packed with restaurants. Many have riverside balcony seating (kawadoko) in summer. October weather is perfect for this. Pick any place that looks good — the atmosphere is the star.
details: 📍 Between Shijo and Sanjo streets, parallel to Kamo River
🍶 Try a local Kyoto sake flight at one of the izakayas
🐟 Kyoto specialties: yudofu (hot tofu), obanzai (Kyoto home-style tapas), kawadoko dining

meals.name: Pontochō Alley Izakaya
meals.description: Atmospheric alley dining along the Kamo River. Pick any spot — the vibe is everything.

activities.title: Evening Walk: Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka Streets
activities.description: Even if Kiyomizu-dera isn't open for special night illumination, the streets leading up to it — Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka — are beautiful at night. Traditional shops, stone steps, and the pagoda lit up against the dark sky.
details: 📍 15-min walk uphill from Gion
📸 Yasaka Pagoda lit up at night = quintessential Kyoto photo
🍵 Starbucks on Ninenzaka is in a renovated 100-year-old townhouse — worth a peek
